learning_outcomes.text: Students know basic knowledge about computer structures and the functioning of microelectronic circuits.
Students can handle the laws of Boolean algebra.
Students master the design and simplification of Boolean circuits.
Students have knowledge in the design of sequential circuits as well as about arithmetic circuits and CMOS transistors.
Students understand the structure and function of a central processing unit (CPU).
Students have basic knowledge in machine language programming.
Students understand fundamental concepts of computer architecture.
Students can follow scientific working methods (recognizing, formulating, solving problems, training abstract thinking skills).
Students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solutions for at least two exercise assignments

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and orally present the solution to at least two of the exercise assignments. The grading is based on a written exam, with scores from 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the B.Sc. Computer Science degree program.
